name: Jackin House
about: Jackin house is Chicago house at its most physical: the swung, bumping strain built on chopped disco and funk loops, filtered vocal stabs and a bassline that never sits still. The name goes back to the mid-1980s, when Chip E., Farley "Jackmaster" Funk and Steve "Silk" Hurley told dancers to jack their bodies over raw drum-machine tracks; the style proper took shape in the 1990s through Cajual and Relief, Paul Johnson, DJ Sneak and Derrick Carter, who made the chopped-sample bump the city's trademark. A British offshoot around Bristol and the Midlands carried it into the 2010s with Sonny Fodera and Low Steppa, cleaner and louder. It remains a working DJ's style, documented mostly on 12-inch singles and mix CDs rather than albums.

albums.title: The House Sound of Chicago
albums.why: The DJ International compilation that exported jack tracks to Britain, with Hurley, Farley and Chip E. alongside the city's first vocal anthems.

albums.title: Hold On to Your Dream
albums.why: Steve Hurley and Keith Nunnally's only album as J.M. Silk, a major-label attempt to make jack tracks into songs that works about half the time.

albums.title: Jack to the Sound
albums.why: Raw, loud and already rapping over the beat, Fast Eddie's debut is the bridge between jack tracks and hip house.

albums.title: No Vocals Necessary
albums.why: The Hot Mix 5 veteran's instrumental statement: drum-machine workouts with the swing that the later jackin producers built their careers on.

albums.title: From the Mind of Lil Louis
albums.why: Built around French Kiss, this is Chicago house with a producer's ambition, equal parts jack, sleaze and song, and still the city's best 1980s album.

albums.title: Blue Funk Files
albums.why: Sneak's Henry Street debut set the filtered-disco template for the next decade, Chicago bump with the loops swept open and shut.

albums.title: Feel the Music
albums.why: The jackin sound's purest album: sampled funk chopped to the bar, a kick that pushes, and not a wasted second across the Peacefrog set.

albums.title: Bump Talkin'
albums.why: Rougher and more tool-like than Feel the Music, this is Johnson in Dance Mania mode, and the tracks were made for a DJ's hands.

albums.title: Higher Power
albums.why: Cajual's singer gets a full-length of gospel-tinged house over Cajmere's bumping productions, with Day by Day and U Got Me Up as the anchors.

albums.title: Home Town Chicago
albums.why: Guidance Recordings' survey of the deeper, swinging second generation, warm chords over a jackin bottom end.

albums.title: San Francisco Sessions Vol. 1
albums.why: The Om Records mix that defined West Coast jackin house, Farina's Chicago bump softened with a little Bay Area haze.

albums.title: Green Velvet
albums.why: Cajmere's alter ego collects Flash, Answering Machine and the rest of his deadpan, jacking tech-house singles for a major label.

albums.title: Squaredancing in a Roundhouse
albums.why: Carter's one proper album turns the jackin bump into songs, with soul vocals, jazz chords and a swing nobody else in Chicago has.

albums.title: Air Farina
albums.why: Farina's studio album stays close to his DJ sets, jackin loops with a downtempo side, and it is the most listenable document of his style.

albums.title: Fabric 56
albums.why: A late-career mix that shows exactly why Carter is the jackin DJ's DJ: three-deck blends, Chicago classics and swing throughout.

albums.title: Fabric 62
albums.why: Sneak at full stride, a mix of chunky disco-house tools that reads as a manifesto for the bump against the minimal decade.

albums.title: Hardcore Traxx: Dance Mania Records 1986-1997
albums.why: Strut's survey of the Dance Mania label, where jack tracks hardened into ghetto house, with Paul Johnson, DJ Funk and the raw originals.

albums.title: Frequently Flying
albums.why: The Defected album that made the UK jackin sound a festival proposition, polished and vocal-led, more pop than Chicago.

albums.title: Rise
albums.why: Fodera's second album leans further toward radio house, but the bounce of his early jackin singles still carries the best tracks.

note: Jackin house lives on 12-inch singles and DJ mixes, so this shelf stops at nineteen records rather than padding with guesses.
